title: ISS cricket experiment found microgravity-exposed larvae hatched earlier than ground controls
summary_full: In 2005, scientists examined cricket reproduction on the International Space Station, where embryos grew under microgravity conditions. Interestingly, larvae emerged sooner than those on Earth, suggesting that microgravity affects developmental speed while preserving key neural structures. This research is vital for comprehending how life forms adjust to lesser gravitational forces, expanding our knowledge of development beyond Earth.
